chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what is killed by the sling-stone and the rock, is it permissible to eat from it? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَ يُؤْكَلُ: Is it permissible to eat; a standard legal query formula.
key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah; a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْبُنْدُقُ: Sling-stone; a projectile used in hunting, often implying blunt force rather than a sharp cut.
key_terms.الْحَجَرُ: The rock; used here to denote blunt force killing.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat animals killed by a sling or rock in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that game killed by blunt force (*bunduq* or *hajar*) is not permissible for consumption, distinguishing it from the standard method of slaughter. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the efficacy of the killing method, where the projectile must cause death directly rather than merely stunning or crushing the animal, ensuring the meat remains *tayyib* (pure).
